papers.title: One-Shot Human Motion Transfer via Occlusion-Robust Flow Prediction and Neural Texturing
papers.citation: Yuzhu Ji, Chuanxia Zheng, Tat-Jen Cham. One-Shot Human Motion Transfer via Occlusion-Robust Flow Prediction and Neural Texturing. IEEE Trans. Multim., 27, 3939–3952, 2025.
papers.venue: IEEE Trans. Multim.
papers.authors: Yuzhu Ji, Chuanxia Zheng, Tat-Jen Cham
papers.abstract: Human motion transfer aims at animating a static source image with a driving video. While recent advances in one-shot human motion transfer have led to significant improvement in results, it remains challenging for methods with 2D body landmarks, skeleton and semantic mask to accurately capture correspondences between source and driving poses due to the large variation in motion and articulation complexity. In addition, the accuracy and precision of DensePose degrade the image quality for neural-rendering-based methods. To address the limitations and by both considering the importance of appearance and geometry for motion transfer, in this work, we proposed a unified framework that combines multi-scale feature warping and neural texture mapping to recover better 2D appearance and 2.5D geometry, partly by exploiting the information from DensePose, yet adapting to its inherent limited accuracy. Our model takes advantage of multiple modalities by jointly training and fusing them, which allows it to robust neural texture features that cope with geometric errors as well as multi-scale dense motion flow that better preserves appearance. Experimental results with full and half-view body video datasets demonstrate that our model can generalize well and achieve competitive results, and that it is particularly effective in handling challenging cases such as those with substantial self-occlusions.

papers.title: CPNet: 3D Semantic Relation and Geometry Context Prior Network for Multi-Organ Segmentation
papers.citation: Yuzhu Ji, Mingshan Sun, Yiqun Zhang, Haijun Zhang. CPNet: 3D Semantic Relation and Geometry Context Prior Network for Multi-Organ Segmentation. ECAI 2024 - 27th European Conference on Artificial Intelligence, 19-24 October 2024, Santiago de Compostela, Spain - Including 13th Conference on Prestigious Applications of Intelligent Systems (PAIS 2024), 392, 153–160, 2024.
papers.venue: ECAI 2024 - 27th European Conference on Artificial Intelligence, 19-24 October 2024, Santiago de Compostela, Spain - Including 13th Conference on Prestigious Applications of Intelligent Systems (PAIS 2024)
papers.authors: Yuzhu Ji, Mingshan Sun, Yiqun Zhang, Haijun Zhang
papers.abstract: Automatic multi-organ segmentation of the abdominal region is a critical yet challenging task in computer-aided medical image analysis. Recent advances in CNN- and Transformer-based encoder-decoder models tend to implicitly learn context features by using enhanced effective receptive fields to capture local and global range dependencies. However, due to the complex anatomical structure, those models cannot recover the anatomical topology properly and result in broken organs with inaccurate semantic labels. Therefore, in this paper, by considering the anatomy priors of multi-organs, we propose a Context Prior Network, namely CPNet, which integrates the 3D context semantic relations and geometry priors as explicit anatomical constraints. Specifically, a Semantic Relation Prior Propagation (SRPP) module is designed to propagate the semantic relations between voxels progressively. Moreover, a Multiple Context Prior Prediction (MCPP) module is adopted to preserve the accurate shape and topology by recovering 3D contours and surface normal. Experimental results demonstrate our proposed model outperforms state-of-the-art models for multi-organ segmentation on Abdomen CT and MRI datasets, especially for recovering organs with correct semantic labels and anatomical structures.

papers.title: QGRL: Quaternion Graph Representation Learning for Heterogeneous Feature Data Clustering
papers.citation: Junyang Chen, Yuzhu Ji, Rong Zou, Yiqun Zhang, Yiu-ming Cheung. QGRL: Quaternion Graph Representation Learning for Heterogeneous Feature Data Clustering. Proceedings of the 30th ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining, KDD 2024, Barcelona, Spain, August 25-29, 2024, 297–306, 2024.
papers.venue: Proceedings of the 30th ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining, KDD 2024, Barcelona, Spain, August 25-29, 2024
papers.authors: Junyang Chen, Yuzhu Ji, Rong Zou, Yiqun Zhang, Yiu-ming Cheung
papers.abstract: Clustering is one of the most commonly used techniques for unsupervised data analysis. As real data sets are usually composed of numerical and categorical features that are heterogeneous in nature, the heterogeneity in the distance metric and feature coupling prevents deep representation learning from achieving satisfactory clustering accuracy. Currently, supervised Quaternion Representation Learning (QRL) has achieved remarkable success in efficiently learning informative representations of coupled features from multiple views derived endogenously from the original data. To inherit the advantages of QRL for unsupervised heterogeneous feature representation learning, we propose a deep QRL model that works in an encoder-decoder manner. To ensure that the implicit couplings of heterogeneous feature data can be well characterized by representation learning, a hierarchical coupling encoding strategy is designed to convert the data set into an attributed graph to be the input of QRL. We also integrate the clustering objective into the model training to facilitate a joint optimization of the representation and clustering. Extensive experimental evaluations illustrate the superiority of the proposed Quaternion Graph Representation Learning (QGRL) method in terms of clustering accuracy and robustness to various data sets composed of arbitrary combinations of numerical and categorical features. The source code is opened at https://github.com/Juny-Chen/QGRL.git.

papers.title: CFNet: A Coarse-to-Fine Framework for Coronary Artery Segmentation
papers.citation: Shiting He, Yuzhu Ji, Yiqun Zhang, An Zeng, Dan Pan, Jing Lin, Xiaobo Zhang. CFNet: A Coarse-to-Fine Framework for Coronary Artery Segmentation. Pattern Recognition and Computer Vision - 6th Chinese Conference, PRCV 2023, Xiamen, China, October 13-15, 2023, Proceedings, Part V, 14429, 431–442, 2023.
papers.venue: Pattern Recognition and Computer Vision - 6th Chinese Conference, PRCV 2023, Xiamen, China, October 13-15, 2023, Proceedings, Part V
papers.authors: Shiting He, Yuzhu Ji, Yiqun Zhang, An Zeng, Dan Pan, Jing Lin, Xiaobo Zhang
papers.abstract: Coronary Artery (CA) segmentation has become an important task to facilitate coronary artery disease diagnosis. However, existing methods have not effectively addressed the challenges posed by the thin and complex structure of CA, leading to unsatisfactory performance in grouping local detailed vessel structures. Therefore, we proposed a novel coarse-to-fine segmentation framework, namely CFNet, to refine the CA segmentation results progressively. The global structure targeting module aims to capture the spatial structure of the CA by introducing dilated pseudo labels as supervision. In addition, a lightweight transformer-based module is designed to refine the coarse results and produce more accurate segmentation results by capturing the long-range dependencies. Our model exploits both local and global contextual features by integrating a convolutional neural network and visual Transformer. These two modules are cascaded using a center-line patching strategy, which filters out unnecessary features and mitigates the sparsity of CA annotation. Experimental results demonstrate that our model performs well in CA segmentation, particularly in handling challenging cases for fine vessel structures, and achieves competitive results on a large-scale dataset, i.e., ImageCAS, in comparison to state-of-the-art methods.

courses.title: Principles and Application of AI Chip
courses.body: This course takes several typical applications in the field of AI computing, and focus on the basic principles and system optimization methods involved in instruction set, compiler and software stack from software algorithm to computer architecture. To understand the design process of AI computing from the perspective of system. The purpose of this course is to develop students' basic skills in designing and using relevant compilers and software stacks and system optimization methods based on an AI computing architecture.

courses.title: Machine Learning and Data Mining
courses.body:
Since the dawn of the 21st century, informatization and digitization have transformed the world, with information technology permeating every facet of human society. The rapid development and widespread adoption of technologies such as the Internet, the Internet of Things (IoT), cloud computing, and mobile internet have led to an explosion of data. As the country with the largest number of internet and mobile internet users, China stands at the forefront of this revolution, boasting abundant data resources and a thriving application market, giving it unique advantages in big data development.

The integration of big data and machine learning analysis has introduced unprecedented opportunities in economic research, enabling the study of long-term processes, large-scale spatial patterns, and rapid economic dynamics. Leveraging data from sources such as the internet, social networks (e.g., WeChat and Weibo), IoT, and geographic information systems, economic analysis now reaches new depths and broader scopes.

Through this course, students will learn to apply machine learning techniques to analyze and mine big data, addressing real-world economic challenges. The course emphasizes building practical problem-solving skills and enhancing data analysis capabilities, laying a strong foundation for developing professional expertise.

courses.title: Computer Vision
courses.body:
Computer vision is a core area of artificial intelligence, enabling machines to analyze and interpret visual data from the world, driving advancements in autonomous vehicles, augmented reality, medical diagnostics, and robotics. This course introduces core concepts such as image acquisition, processing, feature extraction, segmentation, and 3D reconstruction, with practical applications in depth estimation and panoramic stitching.

Hands-on experiments utilize OpenCV for tasks like object detection and motion tracking, alongside deep learning frameworks such as TensorFlow, PyTorch or Mindspore for modern applications like scene understanding and image generation. Students will gain practical skills through projects, preparing them to address contemporary challenges in computer vision.

researchInterests: 以人为中心的多模态视频分析与合成
视觉显著性推理与定位

researchSummary.en: My research focuses on computer vision and machine learning, particularly visual intelligence that perceives, represents, reasons about, and interacts with the physical world. Current interests include human-centric multimodal video analysis and synthesis, 6D object pose estimation, visual saliency reasoning and grounding, medical image segmentation, and embodied AI.
researchSummary.zh: 我的研究主要围绕计算机视觉与机器学习展开，关注能够感知、表征、推理并与物理世界交互的视觉智能。当前研究方向包括以人为中心的多模态视频分析与合成、物体六维位姿估计、视觉显著性推理与定位、医学图像分割及具身智能。

zh: 姬玉柱，博士、博士后，广东工业大学计算机学院青年百人 A 类副教授、硕士生导师，IEEE 高级会员。2019 年博士毕业于哈尔滨工业大学，2020 年赴新加坡南洋理工大学计算机科学与工程学院开展博士后研究，2022 年入职广东工业大学。
主要研究方向为计算机视觉、视频分析与合成、人体动作迁移、物体位姿估计、显著性物体检测、医学图像分割等。
累计发表论文 40 余篇，包括 IEEE TNNLS、TMM、TCYB、Information Sciences，以及 KDD、IJCAI、ECAI 等高水平期刊与会议，并申请多项发明专利。
主持国家级、省部级科研项目 4 项，参与科技部重点研发计划项目 1 项、省部级项目 1 项。
en: I am Yuzhu Ji, an Associate Professor and master's supervisor at the School of Computer Science and Technology, Guangdong University of Technology (GDUT), supported by GDUT's Young Hundred Talents Program (Tier A), and a Senior Member of IEEE. I received my Ph.D. from Harbin Institute of Technology in 2019, began postdoctoral research at the School of Computer Science and Engineering, Nanyang Technological University, Singapore, in 2020, and joined GDUT in 2022.
My research interests include computer vision, video analysis and synthesis, human motion transfer, object pose estimation, salient object detection, and medical image segmentation.

I have published over 40 papers in leading journals and conferences, including IEEE TNNLS, TMM, TCYB, Information Sciences, KDD, IJCAI, and ECAI, and have filed multiple invention patent applications.
My research is supported by the National Natural Science Foundation of China (NSFC) and the Natural Science Foundation of Guangdong Province.
